# Microsoft Azure Hybrid Compute management client library for .NET

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Hybrid Compute resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Hybrid Compute management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.HybridCompute
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Hidden private-link validation names forward through a mockable subscription surface
proposals.explanation: Adds sync/async GetValidationDetailsPrivateLinkScope subscription extensions with receiver null checks and corresponding mockable aliases forwarding location, privateLinkScopeId and cancellation to GetValidationDetails/Async. The different names are not overloads of GetValidationDetails.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The extension and mockable alias bodies are explicit in Custom/Extensions outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Hidden doubled license-validation names forward the existing operation
proposals.explanation: Adds sync/async ValidateLicenseLicense subscription extensions and mockable aliases forwarding WaitUntil, data and cancellation to ValidateLicense/Async. They return the delegated typed operation without implementing new polling or result transformation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These distinct public names and delegation bodies are handwritten in Custom extension/mocking partials.

proposals.subtype: ArcSettings update facade converts input and output models around a scoped resource
proposals.explanation: The hidden extension/mockable UpdateSetting pair validates scope strings/input, builds a settings-resource ID and updates using ArcSettingsData. Conversion stringifies nullable Guid tenant IDs, builds nested gateway/settings objects when present and supplies null raw data; reverse conversion returns null for null data and uses Guid.TryParse, yielding null for an unparseable tenant string.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The request/response facade and both concrete model conversions are explicitly implemented in the Custom resource-group partials.

proposals.subtype: Hidden resource-group machine Get forwards a string expand parameter
proposals.explanation: Adds sync/async GetHybridComputeMachine extensions and mockable methods accepting machineName and optional string expand, forwarding them to GetHybridComputeMachines().Get/GetAsync with cancellation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit extension/mocking facades are in Custom/Extensions, not generated method listings.

proposals.subtype: Resource-level profile creation delegates to a parent-bound cached collection
proposals.explanation: Adds hidden sync/async CreateOrUpdate on the license-profile resource, obtaining a cached HybridComputeLicenseProfileCollection bound to Id.Parent and forwarding WaitUntil, data and cancellation. The operation itself is not reimplemented.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The parent-scoped collection delegation is supplied in Custom/HybridComputeLicenseProfileResource.cs.

proposals.subtype: Three-argument identifier helper supplies the default profile name
proposals.explanation: Adds a hidden CreateResourceIdentifier(subscriptionId,resourceGroupName,machineName) overload forwarding those arguments and the literal default to the four-argument overload.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The fixed profile-name adapter is explicitly implemented in the Custom resource partial.

proposals.subtype: Full-data update overloads construct a license patch
proposals.explanation: Adds hidden sync/async Update overloads accepting HybridComputeLicenseData and forwarding a constructed patch with unchanged WaitUntil/cancellation. Null data produces an empty patch; nonnull data copies LicenseType, selected nested license details and tag entries, mapping LicenseCoreType to patch.Type.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit data-valued overloads and ConvertToPatch body are handwritten in Custom/HybridComputeLicenseResource.cs.

proposals.subtype: Machine accessor returns a cached default-profile resource
proposals.explanation: Adds a hidden GetHybridComputeLicenseProfile method constructing a cached profile resource from stored subscription, resource-group and machine names using the captured three-argument identifier helper that supplies default.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The cached resource creation is explicit in the Custom machine resource, and the identifier helper is supplied in the same request.

proposals.subtype: Public ResourceData-derived settings model supplies constructors and raw-data state
proposals.explanation: Defines ArcSettings deriving from ResourceData, with an empty public constructor and a public metadata/Guid-tenant/gateway/raw-data constructor. The latter delegates ARM metadata to base, assigns both settings and retains the supplied raw-data dictionary reference.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete public model and constructor bodies are supplied in Custom/Models/ArcSettings.cs outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Get-only Guid tenant ID declares a nested properties mapping
proposals.explanation: Declares public get-only Guid? TenantId with WirePath("properties.tenantId"), exposing a typed flattened property rather than a string-valued public declaration.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The typed property and active nested wire-path mapping are explicitly supplied in the Custom model.

proposals.subtype: Gateway identifier property declares a nested gateway-properties path
proposals.explanation: Declares public read/write ResourceIdentifier GatewayResourceId with WirePath("properties.gatewayProperties.gatewayResourceId"). The model's separate captured writer implements its conditional JSON emission.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit property and active mapping are supplied in Custom/Models/ArcSettings.cs.

proposals.subtype: Settings writer nests fields and omits the tenant ID in wire format
proposals.explanation: Implements JSON object writing, routes IUtf8JsonSerializable through wire options, checks J/W format and invokes the base writer. It always opens properties.gatewayProperties, writes a defined gateway ID and writes a defined TenantId only outside W format. No local raw-data dictionary emission appears in this writer.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The interface wiring and complete nested-property writer are handwritten in Custom/Models/ArcSettings.Serialization.cs.

proposals.subtype: Settings JSON reads adapt the data model's tenant string to nullable Guid
proposals.explanation: IJsonModel.Create delegates parsing to ArcSettingsData then converts it to ArcSettings, returning null for null data and nullable Guid from Guid.TryParse, with null raw-data storage. The reverse helper stringifies TenantId and constructs nested settings/gateway models with null raw data, but no caller of that reverse helper is present in the captured partials.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The serializer's read delegation and its own conversion helpers are explicit in Custom source, separate from the similar resource-group helper implementation.

proposals.subtype: Persistable settings support BinaryData writing and delegated JSON-model reading
proposals.explanation: Implements IPersistableModel writing via a MemoryStream/Utf8JsonWriter, flushes and returns BinaryData bytes; Create parses BinaryData and converts ArcSettingsData's deserialized result through the captured adapter. GetFormatFromOptions returns J; read format validation inside the delegated data deserializer is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit persistable-model implementations and byte/JSON bridge are handwritten in the Custom serialization partial.

proposals.subtype: Hidden settings factory accepts a nullable Guid tenant
proposals.explanation: Adds a hidden ArcSettings factory with optional ARM metadata, Guid? tenantId and ResourceIdentifier gatewayResourceId, constructing the captured public model with null serializedAdditionalRawData.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The factory's typed signature and constructor call are in Custom/Models/ArmHybridComputeModelFactory.cs.

proposals.subtype: Private-endpoint factory wraps the identifier and materializes group IDs
proposals.explanation: Adds a hidden factory taking ResourceIdentifier privateEndpointId, constructing PrivateEndpointProperty around it, passing connection fields and converting groupIds to a new List<string> or an empty list when null, with null additional raw-data arguments.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit model adaptation and collection materialization are supplied in the Custom factory.

proposals.subtype: ESU factory accepts assigned-license data and initializes its key collection
proposals.explanation: Adds a factory passing assignedLicense and license-assignment fields into LicenseProfileMachineInstanceViewEsuProperties, using an empty ChangeTrackingList<EsuKey> for null keys or a new List<EsuKey> for supplied keys and null additional raw-data storage.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The factory signature, explicit assigned-license argument and list construction are implemented in the Custom model factory.

proposals.subtype: Machine factory builds nested properties from flattened optional inputs
proposals.explanation: Adds a flattened machine factory that defaults tags/resources, creates MachineProperties only when one of the checked property inputs is nonnull, builds storage/cloud/network submodels, materializes supplied enumerables into lists and passes null for selected unexposed fields/raw-data bags before constructing HybridComputeMachineData.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete flattening, null-gated nested construction and collection adaptation are handwritten in the Custom factory.

proposals.subtype: Hidden machine factory overload supplies default hardware-profile arguments
proposals.explanation: Adds a hidden flattened machine factory overload omitting hardwareProfile, storageDisks and firmwareProfile, forwarding the remaining inputs to the captured broader factory with those three arguments set to default.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The distinct overload and its explicit default-argument adaptation are supplied in the Custom factory.

proposals.subtype: License model factory supplies default tags and optional license fields
proposals.explanation: Adds a HybridComputeLicense factory with optional metadata, provisioning state, Guid tenant, license type and details; null tags become a ChangeTrackingDictionary and the constructor receives null additional raw-data storage.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit factory body is in Custom/Models outside Generated; the claim about a prior Models-namespace API is not needed to observe it.

decisions.reason: The Custom extension methods at 21-36 delegate to mockable methods at 19-28, which in turn call GetValidationDetails/Async. The different public method names and hidden attributes support a handwritten name-preserving shim; the comments' claims about earlier GA surface are not independently verified.

The Custom extension methods at 42-57 and mockable methods at 34-43 provide distinct ValidateLicenseLicense/Async names and forward to ValidateLicense/Async. This is a handwritten API shim, not a custom LRO implementation; historical GA provenance remains a source-comment claim.

The extension facade at 64-81 forwards to mockable methods at 21-52, which construct a scoped settings resource, call Update/Async and wrap converted ArcSettings results. The cited conversion at 54-77 maps Guid and gateway properties in both directions. This is one facade-plus-adapter behavior, distinct from ArcSettings' own serializer implementation.

The Custom extension at 87-104 forwards the machine name and string expand parameter to the mockable methods at 83-94; those invoke the machines collection Get/GetAsync. These are handwritten convenience facades, while any older GA signature asserted by comments is not independently established.

The two Custom resource methods at 22-26 and 33-37 obtain a collection scoped to Id.Parent through GetCachedClient and forward the full operation arguments. The code changes the callable resource-level surface, not the LRO polling implementation.

The three-argument identifier helper at 44-46 supplies the literal default profile name to its four-argument overload. This is a distinct handwritten identifier convenience overload; the claimed history of the old API is only documented in a comment.

The Custom Update/UpdateAsync overloads at 20-31 accept full license data and use the explicit ConvertToPatch mapping at 33-55 before forwarding. The null-input empty patch and copied fields/tags are visible in source; no polling change is implied.

GetHybridComputeLicenseProfile at 16-20 uses GetCachedClient and a profile identifier built from the machine resource's stored Id components. The cited helper at 44-46 supplies the default profile name; its standalone overload is already counted separately, not recounted as another accessor.

The Custom ArcSettings partial at 13-35 defines a ResourceData-derived public model with two constructors and state for tenant, gateway and a raw-data dictionary. This is a handwritten model surface; the stored raw-data field alone does not demonstrate round-trip preservation.

The source at 38-39 shows a nullable Guid property with a nested WirePath, and the captured adapter converts a string tenant ID to Guid. This is typed projection of a model property, not evidence that TenantId aliases another public property; use the existing model-property-typed-projection pattern without changing the cited symbol or source identity.

decisions.reason: The Custom model at 42-43 declares a read/write ResourceIdentifier gateway property mapped to properties.gatewayProperties.gatewayResourceId. The separate writer at 42-48 conditionally emits it, as the proposal notes, without needing to count serialization twice.

The Custom serializer at 13-51 explicitly wires JSON writing, validates its format, delegates base writing and emits nested properties. TenantId is conditional on Format not being W, whereas gatewayProperties is always opened and its ID is conditionally written; only the local writer's lack of raw-data emission is observable.

IJsonModel.Create at 53-54 delegates to ArcSettingsData, and the conversion at 87-96 maps the deserialized string tenant ID to nullable Guid and constructs ArcSettings. The reverse helper at 73-85 is present but no call to that helper appears in these captures, so its runtime use is not inferred.

The handwritten persistable methods at 56-71 write a JSON model to BinaryData, parse BinaryData via JsonDocument and delegate deserialization through ArcSettingsData; GetFormatFromOptions returns J. The generated data model's internal validation and any unsupported formats on read are outside supplied evidence.

The Custom model factory at 22-24 exposes a hidden, nullable-Guid ArcSettings constructor adapter for mocking and passes null raw-data storage. The cited signature and body support this distinct factory API, not the historical AutoRest API asserted in documentation.

The hidden factory at 32-34 wraps a ResourceIdentifier in PrivateEndpointProperty and materializes groupIds into a new list or empty list. This is an explicit handwritten mocking-factory adapter; the comment's backward-compatibility history is not independently proven.

The factory at 38-39 accepts assignedLicense and license-assignment data, creates the ESU model and chooses a new list for supplied keys or ChangeTrackingList for absent keys. It is an explicit Custom factory method, not evidence by itself of any earlier generated factory signature.

The full Custom factory signature at 43 and body at 44-101 show flattened optional machine inputs, conditional creation of nested MachineProperties and typed collection materialization. A single factory-shape finding covers this body, rather than counting each field/default as another customization.

The separate full overload signature at 107-109 omits three hardware/storage inputs and forwards explicit defaults to the broader factory. That is a distinct handwritten overload, although its claimed AutoRest origin is documented only by a comment.

The Custom license factory at 113-129 supplies optional license fields, initializes null tags with ChangeTrackingDictionary and calls the model constructor with null additional raw-data storage. The code supports the factory instance but not the comment's assertion about an older Models-namespace API.
